questions.q: What are the three pillars of observability?
o: Metrics, traces and logs
CPU, memory and disk
Unit, integration and end-to-end tests
Alerts, dashboards and tickets
questions.w: Metrics show that something is wrong, traces show where, and logs show why. Correlate them with trace ids.

o: A vendor-neutral metrics facade with many registries
A new logging framework that replaces SLF4J and Logback
A message broker that carries events between services
A database driver that stores metrics inside a relational table
questions.w: Spring Boot Actuator auto-configures it. You record metrics once and export them to your chosen backend.

questions.q: Which is a high-cardinality tag you should avoid on a metric?
o: `userId` or `accountNumber`
`status`, with a handful of values
`method`, such as GET or POST
`outcome`, success or failure
questions.w: Each distinct tag combination creates a new time series. Unbounded values can overwhelm the metrics backend.

questions.q: What is the difference between a liveness and a readiness probe?
o: Liveness restarts a stuck app; readiness pauses its traffic until ready
Liveness checks the database and readiness checks the CPU
Readiness restarts the pod and liveness routes traffic
Both are the very same endpoint
questions.w: Do not put slow dependency checks in liveness, or a database outage will restart every healthy pod.

questions.q: How do you follow one request through five services?
o: Propagate a trace id and view the spans in a tracing tool
Search the logs of each service by timestamp alone
Restart each service one after another in order
Add an extra database query to every one of the services
questions.w: Micrometer Tracing and OpenTelemetry propagate the W3C `traceparent` header and create spans automatically for HTTP and messaging.

questions.q: What is the MDC used for in logging?
o: It adds context like a trace id to each log line
It rotates the log files whenever they grow too large
It encrypts the log output before it is written to disk
It chooses the active log level for each class at run time
questions.w: Spring Boot with tracing puts `traceId` and `spanId` in the MDC so every log line can be tied to a trace.

questions.q: Which four signals does Google's SRE guidance call the golden signals?
o: Latency, traffic, errors and saturation
CPU, memory, disk and network
Uptime, cost, users and revenue
Logs, metrics, traces and events
questions.w: They give a compact health view of any service. Alert on symptoms that users feel rather than on every cause.

o: A reliability target, e.g. 99.9% of requests under 500 ms
A log retention policy for every node of the cluster
A special kind of load balancer placed in front of services
A contract clause that lists fixed financial penalties only
questions.w: The gap between 100% and the SLO is the error budget, which guides how much risk the team can take with releases.
